positive_findings: Independent exact-source VCS recompilation reproduces the production 96 vectors, 96 outputs, 212 accepted beats, 208 macro requests, 8,832 lane checks, 63 exact vector-start interval checks, four escapes, 13 stall cycles and all six nonzero SVA covers.

Independent boundary attacks cover widths 8, 9, 10 and 11. In all four cases the last legal payload bit is accepted with correct sign extension, while the immediately following first padding bit causes same-cycle quarantine and a registered sticky fault with no following macro request.

The r2 registered downstream-fault boundary removes the r1 self-feedback timing loop. Across the r2 DC log and every report, TIM-209, OPT-150, ELAB-312 and Error counts are zero; the superseded r1 evidence contains one TIM-209 and six OPT-150 occurrences.

The sealed flattened DC evidence manifest verifies and independently reduces to 15,295.644056 um2, 19,042 cells, 15,644 combinational cells, 3,398 sequential cells, zero macros, +0.4516 ns setup slack and +0.0000 ns hold slack at the frozen 3 ns logic-only cut.

Independent arithmetic confirms the integrated logic is 287.279992 um2 (1.843556389771%), 365 cells (1.880764672541%), 12 sequential cells (0.351906158358%) and 353 combinational cells (2.206663749453%) below the separately synthesized M133+M137 sums. This is a synthesis-integration diagnostic, not a total-accelerator comparison.

Source-cone inspection and clean DC loop checks agree: assembler_protocol_error reaches frontend quarantine only through downstream_fault_q on the next edge. The remaining response-ready to request-ready path is feed-forward because response_valid derives from registered pending/skid state and the macro response, not current request_ready.

findings.title: M137 reset-epoch alias is inherited and silently corrupts a complete M138r2 output vector
findings.observation: M138r2 instantiates unchanged M137. M137 resets next_token_q to zero and has neither an external macro flush acknowledgement nor a generation bit. The independent attack accepts an old token-0 request, resets before its response, accepts a new token-0 width-8 request, returns legal-looking stale token-0 data, and completes the new vector. M138r2 emits the new tag with the stale payload bit and protocol_error remains zero.
findings.impact: Reset with an outstanding macro response can silently contaminate packed weights rather than fail closed. The production reset_recoveries=6 only recover after completed attacks and do not test an in-flight external response.
findings.required_fix: Before macro-wrapper admission, add macro_flush_req/flush_ack and hold beat_ready low until stale responses are invalidated, or freeze and assert a truly atomic macro+frontend reset. Add an epoch/generation identity that cannot alias across reset, and replay reset at request, return, skid and final-assembly phases.

findings.title: The one-cycle token-echo macro remains behavioral and aggregate
findings.observation: The port cut has zero SRAM macros. It assumes one aggregate 512-bit response and echoed token exactly one cycle after each accepted read. Per-bank valid/skew, timeout, reset ownership, macro access time and physical bank wiring are outside the design.
findings.impact: The verified 2/2/2/3 schedule is valid under the frozen behavioral contract but does not prove a foundry 16-bank implementation can supply the same return timing or alignment.
findings.minimal_fix: Implement the smallest 16-bank wrapper with per-bank return-valid collection, skew timeout, token/epoch, flush acknowledgement and real macro timing; then rerun VCS, Formality and macro-aware STA.

findings.title: Returned-data padding faults are necessarily post-read and must not be described as zero-read rejection
findings.observation: Metadata/state faults are suppressed before macro_request_valid. Final padding cannot be known until the final 512-bit response returns, so the final read has already occurred. Independent width-complete attacks show the first padding bit is detected and no following read launches, but this does not erase the already-issued final read.
findings.impact: Energy and fault-containment claims differ by fault class. Saying all malformed traffic is rejected pre-SRAM would be false.
findings.minimal_fix: Report metadata-decidable zero-read rejection separately from returned-data padding quarantine. If pre-read padding rejection is required, carry a trusted byte/bit mask or integrity metadata from the producer.

findings.title: Production properties do not encode reset epoch safety or all padding boundaries
findings.observation: Production VCS has one all-ones width-8 padding attack and no outstanding-reset stale-response property. It also has no direct assertion of the 8/9/10/11 first-padding indices or of current valid/ready graph acyclicity. The independent test closes the directed evidence gap for all four widths and exposes the reset defect, but these checks are not yet in the production contract/SVA.
findings.impact: A future RTL edit can regress a width-specific boundary or reset behavior without failing the sealed production regression.
findings.minimal_fix: After repairing reset identity, add four exact boundary pairs, reset-at-every-in-flight-phase assertions/covers, and structural ready/valid loop lint or formal checks to the production suite.

findings.title: The clean DC result is a logic-only target-period check, not paper-ready PPA
findings.observation: The run is flattened standard-cell logic at 3 ns with ideal unpropagated clock, ZeroWireload, zero macro area and zero interconnect area. There is no RTL-to-netlist Formality seal, propagated-clock/topographical timing, SAIF/PTPX energy or SRAM characterization.
findings.impact: The area/cell/slack values are reproducible for this port cut, but do not establish foundry-macro area, routed Fmax, power, energy or silicon feasibility.
findings.minimal_fix: Run Formality using the emitted SVF, instantiate characterized SRAMs, perform macro-aware placed timing with propagated clocks, and run matched SAIF/PTPX before total PPA claims.

findings.title: M138r2 supplies no admitted accelerator speedup baseline
findings.observation: The production check proves beat-level macro issue under ready and vector-start intervals of 2/2/2/3 cycles. The inherited M137 bridge changes isolated first-delivery latency from two cycles to one while both variants remain II1. M138r2 has no matched end-to-end cycle-simulator baseline, and its integration-area delta compares against a sum of two separately optimized logic islands rather than a competing accelerator.
findings.impact: Neither the one-cycle delivery nor the 1.8436% integration area delta is a throughput, physical, full-module or system speedup. Positive slack at a single 3 ns target is not an Fmax measurement.
findings.minimal_fix: Use the same trace, macro model, buffer sizes and resource count for a matched baseline/candidate cycle simulation; report cycles, utilization and stall decomposition separately from bridge latency. Sweep clock constraints or use post-layout STA for frequency claims.

citable_now: Exact-SHA commercial VCS at the behavioral one-cycle aggregate-macro boundary: 96 vectors/outputs, 212 accepted beats, 208 macro requests, 8,832 signed lane checks, four escapes, 63 exact vector-start interval checks and 13 output-stall cycles.
Under that contract, supported widths use exact 2/2/2/3 accepted-beat vector-start intervals, and four metadata-decidable attacks suppress all four corresponding SRAM read attempts.

Independent width-complete evidence: the last legal data bit and first padding bit are distinguished correctly for 8/9/10/11-bit payloads; all four padding faults become sticky and launch no following macro read.

Flattened TSMC28 standard-cell logic-only DC at a 3.000 ns target: 15,295.644056 um2, 19,042 cells, 3,398 sequential cells, setup slack +0.4516 ns, hold slack +0.0000 ns, zero macros, ideal clock and ZeroWireload.
At the same logic-only synthesis cut, integrated M138r2 area is 1.843556% below the separately synthesized M133+M137 area sum; label this only as an integration diagnostic.
not_citable: Any area, timing or PPA number from the failed M138 r1 DC run.
Reset-safe macro integration or silent-stale-response immunity.
A foundry-SRAM implementation, per-bank skew tolerance, macro-inclusive PPA, routed Fmax, power or energy.
A 2x throughput, module, accelerator or system speedup; the inherited 2-to-1 value is isolated bridge first-delivery latency and steady-state II is unchanged.
All faults are rejected before SRAM; returned-data padding faults are detected only after the final read.
DATE headline or best-paper readiness from M138r2 alone.
ordered_actions: Close the inherited reset-epoch P1 with flush/ack or atomic macro reset plus non-aliasing generation identity.
Add the independent four-width padding boundaries and outstanding-reset attacks to production SVA/VCS.
Implement the minimum characterized 16-bank wrapper with per-bank valid/skew and reset ownership.
Run Formality and macro-aware propagated-clock timing, followed by matched SAIF/PTPX.
Build a matched fixed/dense versus M138r2 cycle-simulator comparison before any speedup statement.
claim_boundary: M138r2 admits exact-SHA fixed-one-cycle behavioral-macro functionality, width-complete signed assembly/padding behavior, an acyclic flattened standard-cell logic timing graph and logic-only area/cell/slack at the frozen 3 ns port cut. It retains one reset-epoch P1 and does not admit reset-safe macro integration, macro-inclusive PPA, power, Fmax, throughput gain, physical speedup, system speedup, headline or best-paper status.
